method: The filter is assembled from fixed libpcap BPF primitives rather than free text. Each enabled condition becomes a host, net, port or portrange term with an optional src or dst qualifier, or a bare protocol keyword; several ports are ORed inside one parenthesised group so they bind correctly against the surrounding and/or join; the TCP flag modes expand to the documented tcp[tcpflags] bit tests, where connection attempts are SYN set with ACK clear; conditions are then joined with and or or and optionally wrapped in not (...) for exclusion. Inputs are validated before assembly: hosts must be IPv4 literals, IPv6 literals or RFC 1123 host names, networks must be CIDR blocks and an IPv4 block with host bits set is rewritten to its masked network address because libpcap rejects unmasked values, ports must be numbers from 1 to 65535, low-to-high ranges or service names, at most twelve, and interface names are limited to the 15-character Linux limit. Combinations that cannot match are reported as warnings rather than silently accepted: ICMP or ARP with ports, an IPv4 protocol keyword with an IPv6 address or the reverse, named hosts that resolve only once at capture start, and a named interface that narrows the capture. The page builds text only: it does not open interfaces, capture, resolve names, store or transmit anything, and the expression shown is exactly what tcpdump hands to libpcap, so matching behaviour is libpcap's own. BPF cannot see application payloads, so a filter selects packets by addresses, ports, protocols and TCP header flags only.

sources.title: tcpdump manual page and pcap-filter(7): the host, net, port, portrange, protocol and TCP flag primitives, the src and dst qualifiers, and the not/and/or boolean grammar used here.
The pcap-filter expression grammar in libpcap: qualifiers bind to the following identifier, which is why multiple port terms are parenthesised before being combined with and.
McCanne and Jacobson, The BSD Packet Filter: a register-based filter program compiled from the expression and applied per packet before it is copied to user space.
libpcap pcap_compile and tcpdump -d: the reference implementations that reject a CIDR block whose host bits are set and that compile each generated expression.
